name: 陳彥安
objective: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of digital logic design with a focus on applications relevant to semiconductor process and equipment engineering. Topics include number systems, Boolean algebra, logic minimisation, combinational circuits, sequential circuits, registers, counters, and finite state machines. Throughout the course, concepts are connected to real equipment scenarios including sensor signal processing, threshold alarms, safety interlocks, process sequence control, and equipment start/stop logic. The course is designed for first-year students without prior electronics or programming background; emphasis is placed on building intuition and practical understanding rather than mathematical derivation.

materials:
Textbook:
1. M. Morris R. Mano and Michael D. Ciletti, Digital Design: With an Introduction to the Verilog HDL, VHDL, and SystemVerilog, 6th ed., Pearson.

References:
1. Charles H. Roth, Jr. and Larry L. Kinney, Fundamentals of Logic Design.
2. Thomas L. Floyd, Digital Fundamentals.
3. Ronald J. Tocci, Neal S. Widmer, and Gregory L. Moss, Digital Systems: Principles and Applications.
4. MIT OpenCourseWare, Semiconductor Manufacturing, selected lecture notes on sensors and signals.
5. Wokwi Arduino Simulator documentation, selected examples for digital input / output demonstrations.
6. PLC open textbook materials on latches, timers, counters, and simple machine control.

Instructor-prepared Materials:
1. Digital Logic in Semiconductor Process Equipment
2. Digital Measurement and Control Signals
3. Interlock and Equipment Sequence Case Study
4. Simple Wokwi / Arduino-based digital logic demonstration worksheets
